questions.question: What color are warning signs?

options.text: Yellow with black lettering or symbols
Blue with white lettering or symbols
Red with white lettering or symbols
White with black lettering or symbols

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black lettering or symbols
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: How should jackets and pants fit for the best protection?

options.text: They should cover your arms and legs completely.
They should be loose and flap in the wind while you ride.
They should only partially cover your arms and legs.
They should be made of wool.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should cover your arms and legs completely. They should fit snugly but allow you to move freely. Leather or synthetic materials offer the best protection in an accident.

questions.question: What should you check about your brakes before riding?

options.text: The brakes make a loud squeaking noise.
The brakes cause friction with the steering.
Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can hold the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Test each brake lever before every ride. Make sure each one feels firm and holds the motorcycle when fully applied.

questions.question: Which item does NOT protect a motorcycle rider?

options.text: A leather jacket
Boots that go over the ankle
A baseball cap that fits snugly
Gloves

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap that fits snugly
questions.explanation: For protection, wear a DOT-approved helmet, eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, boots that cover your ankles, and durable gloves. A baseball cap does not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: What should you do if a friend wants to ride after drinking?

options.text: Let them ride.
Tell them to take quiet roads.
Push their bike over.
Get other friends to talk them out of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get other friends to talk them out of riding.
questions.explanation: Never allow someone to ride after drinking. Do everything you can to stop them. Get other friends to help you convince them not to ride.

questions.question: If stopping will take longer than usual, what should you do?

options.text: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
Decrease the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
Leave the road.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: When riding on slippery surfaces or when stopping takes longer, keep extra distance between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down and let them pass.
Move to the shoulder and stop.
Do not worry about it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up will only make the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, which is NOT required?

options.text: Adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
Give the passenger instructions before riding.
Tell the passenger to keep their feet on the footrests.
Squeeze both riders onto a one-person seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze both riders onto a one-person seat.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have a permanent passenger seat and footrests to carry a passenger. Never try to fit two riders on a one-person seat. Give the passenger clear instructions before you start riding.

questions.question: Before riding, what do you NOT need to check?

options.text: The air pressure in the tires.
Fluid levels.
The turn signals.
Damage to the paint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Damage to the paint.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check tire tread and air pressure, oil and fluid levels, lights, and turn signals. Paint damage is not a safety concern for riding.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider improve their visibility?

options.text: Wear dark-colored clothing.
Turn off the headlight.
Follow other vehicles very closely.
Wear bright-colored clothing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothing with reflective materials to be seen by other drivers. Always use your headlight and use your signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, a jacket should be worn:

options.text: All the time, no matter the weather.
Only when it is cool outside.
Only when it is warm outside.
Only if you will ride for more than 30 minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: All the time, no matter the weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even on hot days. A jacket protects you from the sun and helps prevent dehydration.

questions.question: Which type of clothing helps other drivers see you?

options.text: Dark-colored clothes
Clothes made of synthetic materials
Reflective clothes
A leather jacket

questions.correctAnswerText: Reflective clothes
questions.explanation: Wear bright, reflective clothing. This makes it easier for other drivers to see you and your motorcycle.

questions.question: Can clothing help prevent injuries in a crash?

options.text: No, clothing does not provide protection.
No, clothing is just a personal choice.
Yes, but only if garments are very loose and flap in the wind.
Yes, if pants and a jacket completely cover your arms and legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if pants and a jacket completely cover your arms and legs.
questions.explanation: Proper clothing reduces crash injuries. Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely, are made of strong material, and fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind.

questions.question: What is the main active ingredient in marijuana?

options.text: THC
TMJ
MRT
AAP

questions.correctAnswerText: THC
questions.explanation: THC (tetrahydrocannabinol) is the main active ingredient in marijuana.

questions.question: When should you completely check your motorcycle?

options.text: Before every ride.
Once a week.
Once a month.
Once a year.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle completely before every ride. Motorcycles need more attention than cars.

questions.question: What is the best source of information for your motorcycle?

options.text: The owner's manual.
A general book about motorcycles.
Someone who owns a different motorcycle.
A television show about riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual.
questions.explanation: Read your motorcycle's owner's manual before riding it. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle. The manual has specific information about your bike.

questions.question: If you feel tired while riding, you should:

options.text: Keep riding and hope to wake up.
Ride faster.
Ride on the shoulder.
Stop and rest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest.
questions.explanation: Do not ride if you are tired. On long trips, take a rest break at least every two hours to avoid fatigue.

questions.question: When choosing a lane position, you should think about:

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you.
How many cars are ahead on the road.
Which position makes your trip shorter.
Which position lets you pass more vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that makes you visible to other drivers and gives you enough space between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: What clothing should you wear when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Clothes that completely cover your arms and legs.
Clothes that cover your arms but leave your legs exposed.
Clothes that cover your legs but leave your arms exposed.
Whatever is most comfortable, regardless of safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clothes that completely cover your arms and legs.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that completely cover your arms and legs for proper protection.

questions.question: When downshifting, you should:

options.text: Shift multiple gears at one time.
Shift one gear at a time.
Always shift to neutral first.
Accelerate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: When downshifting, shift down one gear at a time. Ease out the clutch slowly between each shift.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. They tell you the rules you must follow on the road.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should be done:

options.text: Before every ride.
Once a week.
Once a month.
Twice a month.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. It only takes a few minutes and helps you stay safe on the road.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle:

options.text: You may exceed the speed limit until the pass is complete.
You may disregard "No passing zone" markings if the pass was started in a passing zone.
You may pass on the shoulder.
You must complete the pass within the posted speed limits and within a legal passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must complete the pass within the posted speed limits and within a legal passing zone.
questions.explanation: Always pass within posted speed limits. Only pass where it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: Which of the following should you inspect during a pre-ride check?

options.text: The general wear and tread of your tires
The amount of cushion your seat has
The shine of your paint
The wind direction

questions.correctAnswerText: The general wear and tread of your tires
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, oil, fluids, lights, turn signals, brakes, clutch, throttle, mirrors, and horn.

questions.question: A danger of riding next to a row of parked cars is:

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may unexpectedly pull out from the row into your path.
Others may be driving slowly while looking for a parking spot.
The road may be uneven.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may unexpectedly pull out from the row into your path.
questions.explanation: Parked cars are dangerous. A driver may pull out without looking, a door may open into your lane, or a person may step out between cars.
